The one thing that matters most

Anthropic is putting 5% of its shares into the new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit.

Jack Clark says that, together with earlier commitments, roughly 20% of all Anthropic equity will go to the public good, and the share can grow as Anthropic grows.

Jack Clark@jackclarkSF
Between this and our prior commitments, roughly 20% of all Anthropic equity will be dedicated to the public good, and that commitment can grow as Anthropic grows.

We plan to use these funds to ensure more people can share in the benefits of AI, and to increase our ability to provide funding to deal with its risks.
Anthropic@AnthropicAI· Oct 18
We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit.

It will start off with 5% of our shares. For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion.

In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good. Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding.

In the post below, we share more details about our new fund.

Riley Brown@rileybrown · Oct 18

This video was edited with one prompt to Opus 5.5. It analyzed his transcript, searched X for B-roll (Claude Code called Grok Bot for that step) and scraped the clips.

This video was edited with 1 prompt with Opus 5.5.

I uploaded a single video of myself (with many mistakes). Opus went on to:

1. Analyze the transcript
2. Search Twitter for the relevant B-roll (Claude Code literally calls GrokBot for this step)
3. Scrape the Twitter video assets
4. Cut the video based on mistakes and word gaps
5. Build out the Blender scene from a template
6. Build the UI and components of each shot (my Blender scene has 4 shots: a computer, phone, table, and board)
7. It took screenshots of every section, analyzed and fixed them
8. Synced every shot, zoom, and animation to the exact words I say
9. Animated a robot arm placing real logos on the table right when I mention them
10. Drew the whiteboard ending with logos and graphics instead of text
11. Pulled a cutaway from the creator's own video, with his voice
12. Rendered all 3,487 frames on RunPod cloud GPUs in under 20 minutes, for less than $1
13. Put me in the bottom third only when I'm talking, so the B-roll stays full screen
14. Added word-by-word captions, sound effects, and music
15. Uploaded it to my Google Drive, ready to post

Will be making a full youtube video this week explaining it. I want to learn a little more about how cloud rendering works before making video, as well as figuring out what the best provider is. (If you are in cloud rendering space, hit me up)

My goal of the youtube video will not be to make it a copyable skill, rather teach people the foundations so they can be creative and make their own mini-world by which they can make videos from, while understanding what's happening under the hood.

Shout out @_chuckyc @_MaxBlade

Codex took 2.4x longer than Claude Code on a one-line edit: 27.4 s vs 11.6 s. Both got 9 of 9.

So we timed both on the edits everyone asks for all day: add a flag, rename a function, fix a median bug. 3 runs each, high effort, graded by a test neither agent saw.

→ Claude Code, Opus 5.5: 11.6 s, 53K tokens, 3-4 steps, 9/9

Anthropic says an internal Claude research model worked out how five public elliptic-curve encryption seeds were generated in under 30 minutes.

Wes Roth@WesRoth
An internal Claude research model identified how five NIST elliptic-curve seeds were generated in under 30 minutes, according to Anthropic.

These public starting values, including the one behind P-256, came from a pseudorandom-number generator initialized with timestamps from 1997–1998.

Anthropic published code to reproduce the results. Cryptographer Filippo Valsorda independently verified the process, and the researchers chose to donate the $36,864 bounty to the Internet Security Research Group.

The finding clarifies the curves’ origins and strengthens confidence in their security.

Grok @Bot can call restaurants by phone and book you a table
Brian Roemmele@BrianRoemmele· Oct 18
“HUNNY MY GROK BOT CALLED OUR FAVORITE ITALIAN RESTAURANT AND MADE US RESERVATIONS”

I built a Grok Bot whose only job is to pick up the phone and book you a table at restaurant. Literally make the call in a beautiful Grok voice. It is absolutely amazing! And it’s free.

Try it: x.ai/bot/TIMrxLJHbE…

Yesterday I told it "book Gourmet Italia in Temecula, 4 people, tonight, around 7." It found the restaurant's number on its own, asked how flexible we were on time, what name to book under, and what callback number to give. Then it read everything back and waited for my OK before it dialed. One call covers every time that works for us, so there's no back and forth.

When the call ends, it tells me what happened in plain English, quotes what the restaurant actually said, and offers to put the reservation on my calendar. If I don't have a calendar connected, it hands me a file that opens right in Apple Calendar.

A Proposal: Grok Phone

Grok Bot needs its own phone number to make and receive calls. I connected a calling service called ClawCall, and the free tier gave me 30 calls or 30 minutes to start. I have no connection to that company. It's just what I used. Once Grok Bot has a number, it stops being something you type to and becomes something that can actually get things done in the real world. @Grok you need an old tyme phone service, buddy.

I built some guardrails. It never hands over a credit card or deposit info, never leaves voicemails unless you ask, makes one call at a time, and never calls on its own.

And this isn't really about restaurants. Change a few words and the same bot can:

- Book a haircut, a massage, or a dentist cleaning

- Get a tee time or a court reservation

- Check if a hotel has a room or will let you check in early

- Schedule a car service or an oil change

- Call around for quotes from a plumber, an electrician, or a caterer

This is one of many ways I use Grok Bot to build businesses and make life easier. The calls I used to put off for days now take me 30 seconds.

I made it shareable, so you can grab "Call A Restaurant Reservation" and use it yourself.

Pstack v0.15.27 adds a beta skill that builds a new skill plus a formal verification suite for whatever you want checked.

lauren@poteto
pstack v0.15.27 ships with a new skill /create-formal-verification-skill!

it's still in beta, and similar to /create-verification-skill, this is a meta-skill that creates a new skill and formal verification suite based on the characteristics you want to verify. for example, you may want to model state machines and systems with concurrency using TLA+, or use kani in rust to check for undefined behavior.

if you're new to formal verification, think of it as mathematically proving properties and invariants (something that must always be true) or "laws" of your system. usually, this means modeling your programs in a separate language like with TLA+ and then running the solver on that spec. newer approaches like with kani and @bendlang take a different approach where there is no separate language: you write kani in rust, and bend in bend (it's also a programming language, and the proofs are written as laws and expressed in its type system).

historically formal verification never reached mainstream status because of the difficulty in modeling and writing proofs. it's quite difficult to model your business requirements and keep them in sync! but i expect that we will see more innovation in formal verification in the future as being able to formally verifiy that the code does what you intended gives your agents superpowers in writing correct software.

in the meantime though, i've been experimenting with modeling our code with TLA+ and have already found several bugs with the skill created by /create-formal-verification-skill.

try it out and let me know how it goes!
